incident-bot: :rotating_light: on-call page: maya.k - urgent networking incident affecting Private Connectivity for custA in eu-central-1. Pager reason: high error rate to private endpoint via VPC peering. Thread started 2112345678
Maya Kapoor: i'm on it, paging net-eng @jasonliu and @priya.s. Seeing alerts from probes and customer report of 502s to private inference endpoints.
Jason Liu: joining. quick ask — is this via PrivateLink or VPC peering for custA? Chris from SE confirmed they use VPC peering + DX backup.
Chris O'Neill: confirmed — primary path is VPC peering to our eu-central shared VPC, backup over Direct Connect. Customer seeing intermittent connectivity since ~22:40 UTC.
Priya Singh: telemetry: 20% 5xx rate on private endpoints for custA since 22:38. Connection attempts drop after initial SYN, traceroutes show next-hop divergence to a partner ASN.
Maya Kapoor: ok load of logs attached to alert. Can someone run BGP neighbor summary for the peering vpc router? suspect route leak or more-specific coming from customer side.
Jason Liu: running right now: ```show ip bgp summary | include 65055
Neighbor        AS  MsgRcvd MsgSent  TblVer  InQ OutQ  Up/Down  State/PfxRcd
10.10.10.2    65055   123456  123450  789012    0    0  0:32:14   12097
```
Jason Liu: we are receiving ~12k prefixes from the customer's router — that's wrong, they should only announce their /24s + private ranges. I see lots of /32s and unexpected more-specifics.
Maya Kapoor: that matches traceroute — some flows are hitting those more-specifics and getting blackholed locally. Chris, can you confirm any config changes on their side recently?
Chris O'Neill: customer says they deployed an internal NAT gateway update at 22:35 which may have changed route advertisement behavior. They didn't intend to advertise host routes.
Priya Singh: mitigation options: 1) apply inbound route-map to drop unexpected more-specifics from that peer, 2) set BGP community to lower local-preference for those prefixes, 3) fail traffic to DX backup. We should do minimal-impact quick fix first.
Maya Kapoor: agreed. Jason, can you stage a route-map that denies prefix-length >24 and only allows their known prefixes? Post the commands here before applying.
Jason Liu: drafting: ```route-map RM-FILTER-IN permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CUSTA-ALLOWED
route-map RM-FILTER-IN deny 20
! prefix-list
ip prefix-list CUSTA-ALLOWED seq 5 permit 198.18.200.0/24
ip prefix-list CUSTA-ALLOWED seq 10 permit 198.18.201.0/24
! apply
interface VPC-PEER-PEER1
 ip policy route-map RM-FILTER-IN in
```
Maya Kapoor: looks good. Chris, confirm those are the only expected customer prefixes.
Chris O'Neill: yes those /24s are what they own for private endpoints. there are a couple /32 monitoring hosts but customer says those shouldn't be advertised.
Jason Liu: applying in 60s to avoid race with ongoing flows. i'll run a graceful apply and monitor.
ops-bot: deploy-runbook: starting route-map apply on vpc-peering-router-12 at 22:53:20 UTC
Jason Liu: applied. ```Configured route-map RM-FILTER-IN on VPC-PEER-PEER1 in```
Priya Singh: monitoring metrics — error rate dropping: 5xx rate down from 20% -> 4% in 2m. flow logs show previously-misdirected flows now hitting correct next-hop.
Maya Kapoor: good. Can we also shift traffic to DX standby for the few remaining prefixes until the customer fixes their advertisement? Chris coordinate with customer to withdraw the leaks.
Chris O'Neill: customer rolling back NAT change and will stop host-route advertisement. ETA 20m. I'll keep them on the line. Also requested they tag leaked prefixes with community no-export next-hop to avoid re-advert.
Jason Liu: temporary measure: adding route-map to set local-preference 50 for any customer prefixes that are more-specific to prefer DX path. Command preview: ```route-map RM-LOWLP permit 10
 match ip address prefix-list CUSTA-MORESPEC
 set local-preference 50
``` I'll stage but not apply unless we see reappearance.
Maya Kapoor: ok leave staged. Priya keep monitoring, page me and @jasonliu for any regression. I'll update incident status to major and start a post-incident ticket.
incident-bot: incident updated: severity=major, incident_id=INC-2021-4729, runbook=network-route-leak
Priya Singh: graph update: connection successes trending back to normal, p95 latency normalizing. still seeing a handful of flows hitting older next-hop for ~15s bursts.
Jason Liu: I see one noisy peer session flapping, clearing BGP session now to reset learned prefixes: ```clear ip bgp 10.10.10.2 soft in```
Priya Singh: after soft-reset, stale prefixes gone. 5xx rate at 0.7% now. Good.
Chris O'Neill: customer confirms they've reverted the NAT change and withdrew the host routes. They will push a fix to prevent host-route advertisement. asked for RCAs and config samples.
Maya Kapoor: thanks. i'm going to hand this to postmortem owner @chris.o to coordinate RCA with customer and @jasonliu for config change review. Handoff note: oncall rotates in 10m — @priya.s you will take watch for 30m, i'll be offline but reachable if needed.
Priya Singh: taking watch. i'll keep 15m checks and escalate if >1% 5xx in next 30m.
Maya Kapoor: summary for incident ticket: cause — customer-side NAT update caused host-route leak via BGP, effect — more-specifics preferred and some traffic blackholed via VPC peering local routers causing ~20% 5xx. mitigation — applied inbound route-map to drop > /24 ads, soft-reset BGP, staged LP rule, failover option available. customer reverted change; monitoring shows recovery. ACTIONS: customer to implement route-filtering on their edge, we to add defensive inbound filters per-peer and include in runbook.
incident-bot: incident INC-2021-4729 status=mitigated updated_time=2112347200
Chris O'Neill: creating follow-up RFC, will include sample route-map and checklist for custA onboarding. reopening thread in 24h for verification.
Maya Kapoor: thanks everyone. closing live channel, transfer to postmortem thread.
